subject: Post-call recap: Air-gapped deployment qualification — HW & offline ops next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@aegisbio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Air-gapped deployment qualification — HW & offline ops next steps

Hi Asha / Tom —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. If I missed anything, flag it and we’ll correct.

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Deployment mode: fully air-gapped on-prem appliance in your secured colo (no outbound internet from the nodes).
- Security controls: customer-managed HSM for keys, SIEM integration via log export, quarterly vulnerability scans.
- Maintenance windows: preferred monthly 1–3am local (PST) windows; emergency patch process exists.
- Throughput target: ~60 concurrent inference sessions, 20k tokens/min peak.
- Upgrade expectations: on-site upgrade bundle (signed), staged validation, and acceptance testing with our QA checklist.

Open items / clarifying questions for Aegis:
1) Can you confirm whether USB-based physical media is permitted for offline upgrades, or do you require an air-gapped hardware transfer process via sealed laptops?
2) Will there be an on-site engineer with root privileges and network console access during install?
3) Do you have a preferred spare-parts list (power supplies, spare NVMe) or should we propose a minimal kit?
4) Are any external integrations (metrics ship to vendor) allowed over an intermediary jumpbox?

What Redwood will provide next:
- Draft offline MOP (method-of-procedure) and an on-site checklist for site readiness.
- Hardware specification sheet for the appliance (attached: airgap-hw-specs.xlsx).
- A one-page security summary and SOC2 evidence pointers for procurement.

Suggested next steps:
- Asha to confirm answers to the four items above by EOD Monday 8/18.
- Redwood to send the offline MOP and spare-parts recommendation by 8/17 (I’ll attach it).
- Schedule an on-site readiness call week of 8/25 to walk the MOP with your ops team.

Attachments: airgap-hw-specs.xlsx (attached)

Thanks — we’ll stay flexible on the phrasing of the MOP depending on your internal change-control requirements.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference

From: Asha Rao <asha@aegisbio.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Gillespie <tom.g@aegisbio.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 18:05:43 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Air-gapped deployment qualification — HW & offline ops next steps

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the clear recap — this matches our notes. A few clarifications below:

Answers to your open items:
1) Offline media: we do permit USB-attached media for vetted images, however images must be signed and delivered in tamper-evident packaging. We also accept transfer via encrypted external SSD handed to our security team onsite.
2) On-site privileges: yes, a senior systems engineer (Tom) will have root and console access during install windows. He cannot provide remote RDP/SSH access outside of the maintenance window.
3) Spare parts: we don’t have a formal list; please propose a minimal spares kit that includes 1x hot-swap PSU, 2x NVMe (800GB), and 1x spare NIC.
4) Integrations: metrics must not leave the network. We can allow a pull-based export from a validated jumpbox only during maintenance windows.

Additional requests from our security team:
- Please provide a documented upgrade rollback plan (MOP addendum) and a signed checksum for upgrade bundles.
- SOC2 and penetration test summary — if you can point us to the specific artifacts or an owner at Redwood that can provide them, that would speed procurement.

We attached our internal network diagram for the colocated room (aegis-network-diagram.pdf).

Questions for Redwood:
- If we go with an appliance model, what is the supported upgrade cadence (major/minor) and how long is the appliance supported for critical patches?
- If we later opt for a Dedicated capacity model instead of on-prem, what data egress assurance and isolation controls do you provide?

We’re aiming to have procurement and security clear the baseline requirements by the end of month. Please send the MOP and spares list and we’ll review.

Regards,
Asha Rao
Head of IT Operations, Aegis BioSystems
asha@aegisbio.com
Attachment: aegis-network-diagram.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Aug 2025 09:22:11 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-call recap: Air-gapped deployment qualification — HW & offline ops next steps

Jordan / Soojin — forwarding Asha’s clarifications. High-level suggestions before we send the MOP:

- Spares kit: agree with Asha’s ask. I’ll propose: 1x hot-swap PSU, 2x enterprise NVMe (800GB), 1x spare 10Gb NIC, 1x m.2 to NVMe adaptor, sealed USB with signed installer image, and a tamper-evident shipping checklist.
- Upgrades: we support signed offline bundles. Typical cadence: quarterly minor patches (security/bugfixes), major releases 1x/year. Critical CVE patches: we’ll produce a signed hotfix bundle within our SLA for critical severity.
- Rollback: MOP will include a validation + rollback sequence and a checksum verification step.
- Dedicated vs Appliance: Dedicated provides network isolation, private tenancy, and predictable throughput; appliance gives you full physical control and eliminates network egress but requires on-site ops and parts handling.

Action items for Ben/Jordan/Soojin:
1) Ben to draft spares list and MOP addendum (this weekend).
2) Soojin to assemble the SOC2/pen test summary pointer and procurement pack.
3) Jordan to propose available on-site POC dates (week of 8/25).

I’ll start drafting the parts list and attach to the MOP before Jordan sends it externally.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@aegisbio.com>, Tom Gillespie <tom.g@aegisbio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 Aug 2025 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Air-gapped deployment qualification — HW & offline ops next steps

Hi Asha / Tom —

Appreciate the quick responses. Attached is our draft offline MOP and the minimal spares recommendation (redwood-offline-mop.pdf). Highlights and direct answers below to help your security/procurement review quickly: 

- Offline upgrade: signed bundles only; checksums and tamper-evident packaging required. We’ll provide an HMAC-signed manifest and a PGP signature for each bundle.
- Upgrade cadence & support window: quarterly minor patches, annual major releases. Critical hotfixes: 30-day turnaround SLA for security-critical patches (documented in the support annex).
- Rollback plan: step-by-step rollback in the MOP with validation checkpoints and an explicit manual hold step prior to finalizing.
- Spares kit: attached section lists the recommended parts matching Asha’s ask. We will also provide part numbers and Redwood part SKUs.
- Remote fallback options: we can run a limited, hands-off diagnostics session via a customer-controlled jumpbox during maintenance windows; no permanent outbound telemetry will be configured.

Concrete next steps:
1) Please confirm that the spares list in the attached MOP satisfies your procurement needs by 8/20.
2) If accepted, we can schedule an on-site POC for either 8/26 or 8/28 — please let me know which date works for Tom.
3) We’ll also route SOC2 evidence to your security contact. Soojin — can you share the pack and the named owner?

If that looks good I’ll attach the signed NDA and a short SOW addendum for air-gapped deployments to the HubSpot deal (link included).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
Attachments: redwood-offline-mop.pdf
